page: Microsoft Azure D4als_v6 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the Dalv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is limited to 8.0 GB, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between compute and memory performance. The AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core performance, as evidenced by high stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, both placing in the top 25%. However, memory subsystem performance is a significant bottleneck. The Passmark memory score falls into the bottom 10%, and memory bandwidth read-only tests for both small and large blocks register in the bottom 25%. Multi-core performance and multi-threaded decompression tasks remain average, constrained by the 2 physical cores and limited memory bandwidth.

Given its hardware profile, the D4als_v6 offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints or local storage. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing, text processing, and basic web serving. However, it is poorly suited for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference, where its restricted memory bandwidth and capacity lead to degraded performance.
